newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: More N. Korean officials seek to flee - radio.
newsitem.headline: More N. Korean officials seek to flee - radio.

text.p: A senior North Korean defector now in Seoul's Beijing embassy has told a U.S. intelligence official that six or seven senior North Korean figures plan to flee the Stalinist nation, Seoul state radio said on Monday.

Hwang Jang-yop told an official from the U.S Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) that six to seven officials from Pyongyang's ruling Workers' Party wanted to seek political asylum. South Korean officials said they were unaware of the move.
Hwang, a senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, has remained in the South Korean mission in Beijing since Wednesday as China, an ally of Pyongyang, seeks a solution to the impasse.
Korea Broadcasting System reported that Hwang had a 35-minute meeting with the U.S. official at Seoul's consular office hours after he arrived there to seek asylum in South Korea.

U.S. ambassador to the United Nations Bill Richardson said on Sunday Washington was closely watching developments involving North Korean defectors after two suspected North Korean gunmen shot and seriously wounded a prominent North Korean defector near Seoul on Saturday.
Seoul officials said Li Il-nam, the nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's ex-wife, remained in coma on Monday in a hospital in Bundang, just south of Seoul.
